name: Spanish East Indies
alt: Spanish East Indies (Captaincy General of the Philippines)

predecessors.name: Rajahnate of Cebu
predecessors.text: Cebu, where Legazpi planted the first Spanish settlement in 1565; the Captaincy page names 'Rajah Patis of Cebu' as the leader of resistance

predecessors.name: Maynila
predecessors.text: Maynila, captured and renamed Manila in 1571

successors.name: United States of America
successors.text: the Philippines and Guam, ceded by the Treaty of Paris signed 10 December 1898 (in force 11 April 1899)

successors.name: German Empire
successors.text: the remaining Pacific islands (Marianas without Guam, Carolines, Palau), sold on 12 February 1899

successors.name: First Philippine Republic
successors.text: the land that Filipino forces had 'liberated ... from the Spanish' by 1898

capitals.name: Panay (Spanish headquarters at the second settlement)

ledger.x: 1565: Legazpi plants the first Spanish settlement of the Philippines at Cebu.
1569: Legazpi moves the Spanish headquarters from Cebu to Panay.
1571: the Spaniards take Maynila and rename it Manila.
1574: the Philippines become a captaincy general.
1574: Palau enters the East Indies timeline.
1626: a Spanish post in northern Taiwan (Spanish Formosa).
1642: Spanish Formosa lost to the Dutch.

1668: Guam. 'In 1668, Blessed Diego Luis de San Vitores established the first mission on Guam'; the timeline lists the Marianas as 1667-1898. The Captaincy page records that Legazpi 'arrived in Umatac in 1565 and claimed the island of Guam for Spain'.
1851: the Sultan of Jolo acknowledges Spanish sovereignty on paper.
1878: Sulu is again a Spanish dependency from the treaty of 22 July 1878.
1898: the government leaves Manila for Iloilo after the American capture of Manila.
1898: the Philippines and Guam pass to the United States.
1898: Spain's claim over Sulu ends with the cession of the Philippines (Treaty of Paris, 10 December 1898).

wars.name: Spanish-Moro conflict
wars.outcome: The Spaniards held Zamboanga (1635-1663, from 1718), received Basilan (1724), Davao (1849) and Sulu's submission (22 July 1878), and fought for Cotabato and Lanao to the 1890s; 'Moro resistance against Spanish colonial authorities continue until the 1898 US…

wars.name: British occupation of Manila
wars.outcome: Manila occupied October 1762 for twenty months; returned in April 1764 under the 1763 Treaty of Paris; the British 'were unable to extend their conquest outside of Manila'.

wars.name: Dutch-Spanish naval actions in the Philippines
wars.outcome: Naval actions in 1610, 1617 and 1624 and the five Battles of La Naval de Manila in 1646; the page records no territorial change.

wars.name: Philippine Revolution
wars.outcome: Revolution from 23 August 1896; independence declared 12 June 1898; by 1898 'Filipino forces had liberated much of the country' (Spanish colonization page) and Spain ceded the islands to the United States.

wars.name: Spanish-American War (Philippine theatre)
wars.outcome: Battle of Manila 13 August 1898; Treaty of Paris signed 10 December 1898; Spain ceded the Philippines and Guam for $20 million.

certainty.note: Spanish control was a string of settlements and forts; the Cordillera, most of Mindanao and Sulu stayed outside.
The Jolo treaty of 22 July 1878 and the Madrid protocol of 7 March 1885 fix Sulu and North Borneo on paper only; Mindanao's interior was 'nominally under Spanish control'.
The Treaty of Paris fixed a specified line round the archipelago; the German sale of 12 February 1899 named islands, not a line.
